newsitem.title: USA: Fed judge orders Planned Parenthood funding in Mo..
newsitem.headline: Fed judge orders Planned Parenthood funding in Mo..

text.p: Missouri lawmakers violated the "spirit" and the "letter" of a permanent injunction when they voted to eliminate all state aid to Planned Parenthood, a U.S. District Court judge in Kansas City has ruled.

Judge Fernando Gaitan Jr had overturned a state ban on Planned Parenthood funding last year and ruled Monday afternoon that a prohibition approved this year violated constitutional protections as well.

Based on the text of the legislation, and his June 1996 ruling, "implementation of any of the restrictions following the first sentence (of the section) would violate not only the spirit of the amended order, but its letter as well," Gaitan found.
Missouri Attorney General Jay Nixon had asked Gaitan on Friday to clarify whether the prohibition in the new state budget would violate his earlier order.
Gov. Mel Carnahan, who opposed the funding cut, had asked Nixon to seek the clarification.
In his earlier ruling, Gaitan had found no rational basis for distinguishing Planned Parenthood from other eligible recipients for the state family planning funds.

Missouri has appropriated funds for family planning services to low-income women and men who do not qualify for Medicaid benefits since 1993. Planned Parenthood had received reimbursements from 1993 to 1995 before it was excluded in 1996, leading to the federal court dispute.
